<details>
The .SRCINFO file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It specifies the package base, version, architecture, source URLs, and checksums. The sources point to prebuilt binary releases hosted on the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/kanywst/wtfi2), which is consistent with the declared upstream. The SHA-256 checksums are provided for both x86_64 and aarch64 binaries, ensuring integrity verification. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network operations beyond fetching the expected release binaries.

The package provides `wtfi`, conflicts with alternative versions (`wtfi2-git`, `wtfi2`), and sets appropriate build options (`!lto`, `!debug`) likely to avoid issues with precompiled binaries. All fields conform to standard AUR packaging practices. No executable code or commands are present in this file, and it does not perform any actions on its own. It merely describes how to retrieve and validate the binary assets.

As this is a `-bin` package, it is expected that the sources are precompiled binaries with checksums. The use of GitHub Releases for distribution is common and acceptable for such packages. No evidence of tampering, backdoors, or malicious behavior is present in the metadata.
</details>

The sources are architecture-specific tarballs for x86_64 and aarch64, matching the declared upstream. Checksums (sha256sums) are provided for both architectures and are not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified integrity.

The package function extracts and installs the binary, license, and documentation into appropriate system directories using standard `install` commands. No unusual or dangerous operations such as `eval`, `curl|bash`, or runtime code generation are present. All actions are consistent with safe, static binary packaging practices. The use of `!lto` and `!debug` in options is benign and common for binary-only packages.

There is no evidence of obfuscated code, unauthorized network access, or system modification beyond the scope of the application. The source URLs point directly to the project's GitHub releases, which is expected behavior. The package does not modify unrelated system files or install hooks that perform suspicious actions.
